answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A tundra delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A marble check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A haven penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 11207 identities need 11207 bonds of 58 tokens, 1270 dollars of hardware and 7 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
